note: Reel 34: You're the Victim (working title). Draft 3, after two cold reads (n07b, for whoever saw the wallet, added at HQ's note): no replay and no study on screen (the study goes to the caption and the pinned comment). Three men bump you in a market lane and your wallet's gone; whoever you pick goes to jail. Look down: it slipped out of your hand at four seconds and has lain at your feet the whole time. The narrator is the series voice (af_heart). Lines that need a real pause are their own lines. Facts: docs/research.md. n07b: misaki flapped 'spotted' to /spˈɑTᵻd/ ('spodded') in every take, so its t is planned by hand; n07c ('saw it', nothing to flap) is the fallback, and only one of the two is placed. The fresh review: misaki said misdirection /mˌɪsdəɹˈɛkʃən/ ('mis-der-ection'); n09 plans 'mis-dye-' (/dI/), n09b 'mis-di-' (/dɪ/). 'Look down' had its stress on Look; n04b gives down the primary stress. Variants are voiced side by side; one of each is placed.
ref_text: The night was cold and very quiet. Most of the street was asleep, and the lamps hummed over the empty road. Somewhere far away, a train rolled past, and then the silence came back.

lines.text: Whoever you pick goes to jail.
It's been there the whole time.
And whoever you picked is going to jail for bumping into you.
If you spotted it, nobody goes to jail.
lines.text_kokoro: If you [spotted](/spˈɑtᵻd/) it, nobody goes to jail.

lines.text: If you saw it, nobody goes to jail.
It slipped out of your hand four seconds in, while you were face to face with number two.
